_: THE process definition. Phases, cluster statuses, buckets and tiers are CLOSED
enums owned by the kit; every driver (SKILL.md, the Cursor rule, Hektor Console,
a terminal session) renders these names and no others.
Why this file exists: these enums used to be restated in each surface, and they
drifted. `confirm` sat in the ledger's phase list and in no driver's UI, so the
console silently swallowed every confirm event; `resolved-upstream` was collapsed
into `green`, which turned 'someone else already fixed this' into 'we proved this
green'. Buckets never drifted — because kernel.md §5.1 called them a closed enum
in one place and both sides copied that one place. This file is that one place
Consumers: core/ledger.sh validates against the same sets (core/tests/process-
parity-test.sh proves the two agree); INTEGRATION.md documents them for callers.

phases.label: Ingest
phases.summary: Pin the build by @timestamp and pull its FAILED docs.
phases.detail: Anti-stale: build numbers are reused, so the build is resolved by exact name AND timestamp. Ends with a cheap testbox health-check — a broken box invalidates every verdict downstream, so it is checked before anything is clustered.

phases.label: Cluster
phases.summary: Group the failures by a root cause a human recognises.
phases.detail: core/cluster.sh makes a mechanical first cut by exception signature; the driver re-groups it into meaning buckets. Ordered easy-fix first, likely-bug last.

phases.label: Pick
phases.summary: The operator chooses which clusters to take. One decision.
phases.detail: The first of only two human gates. Nothing has been rerun yet — this table is built straight from the ingested report.

phases.label: Confirm
phases.summary: Rerun the picked clusters to separate real failures from flaky ones.
phases.detail: Runs before any edit. A test that passes here was never broken — it is dismissed rather than 'fixed'. This is the slowest phase before a fix exists, which is why it is a phase and not a footnote: the operator is watching a testbox run, not a stalled pick.

phases.label: Fix
phases.summary: Apply the fix to the working tree and compile-check it.
phases.detail: core/apply.sh writes only inside the configured source roots and never commits; core/compile.sh catches a broken edit before it costs a testbox run.

phases.label: Verify
phases.summary: Green-proof on the testbox: pass^N, graded by core/gate.sh.
phases.detail: One green run is not proof — a flaky test passes about half the time, so a single green is the likeliest false 'fixed'. The fixer does not grade its own work: only gate.sh's decision:"accepted" counts.

phases.label: Report
phases.summary: The round's scoreboard. The operator reviews the diff and commits.
phases.detail: The second and last human gate. Converging is not finishing — the operator decides when the triage is over.

proposed.label: Proposed
proposed.meaning: On the table, not yet chosen.

selected.label: Picked
selected.meaning: The operator chose it. Work is owed on it — a session may not end here (I11).

applied.label: Fixing
applied.meaning: A fix is in the working tree, unproven. A session may not end here either (I11). Carries passes/runs once green-proof starts.

green.label: Green
green.meaning: Fixed and proven: gate.sh accepted it over N runs.

flagged.label: Suspected bug
flagged.meaning: The app broke its contract, or the element vanished. Evidence recorded, nothing filed — the kit never opens a ticket.

deferred.label: Deferred
deferred.meaning: Not pursued this round. Reversible on purpose: the operator can ask for it back, and parking here is how a turn ends cleanly.

resolved-upstream.label: Already fixed
resolved-upstream.meaning: Current code already handles it — someone else fixed it. NOT the same claim as `green`: nothing was proven on the box. A driver that renders this as green overstates what the run did.
resolved-upstream.note: The one terminal status that does NOT reopen. green/flagged/deferred are decisions about work, and the operator routinely revisits those. This one is an assertion about current code — kernel §6 says don't re-litigate it. A driver must not offer 'reopen' here: ledger.sh refuses the transition, and the operator gets an error they cannot act on. If the assertion was wrong, the failure resurfaces in the next round's re-cluster on its own.

buckets.label: Easy fix
buckets.meaning: A known recipe applies — overlay dismissal, empty-list guard.

buckets.label: Selector
buckets.meaning: The element still exists under a different locator. Re-locate by a robust sibling, never the golden brittle id.

buckets.label: Visual diff
buckets.meaning: Visual-regression baseline drift. Advisory — a human reviews baseline vs regression.

buckets.label: App changed
buckets.meaning: The app changed intentionally and the test's assumption is stale.

buckets.label: Infra
buckets.meaning: Flaky timing, a per-box confound, or data/flag dependence. Not a code fix.

buckets.label: Likely bug
buckets.meaning: The test is self-consistent and the app broke its contract. Flag it, never 'fix' it.

tiers.label: Moderate
tiers.meaning: Data or assertion resilience, still test-local.

tiers.label: Risky
tiers.meaning: Touches a shared Page/Layout — green-proof must widen to the blast radius.

tiers.label: Investigate
tiers.meaning: Suspected app-bug, or too ambiguous to call.

ledger.note: The kit imposed no path convention, so every caller invented one — two real runs wrote two ledgers for the same build and neither driver could find the other's. `ledger.sh path <build>` resolves this convention; drivers should call it rather than inventing a path.
